focus: /iː/ (meat) vs /ɪ/ (chicken) · /tʃ/ (cheese) vs /ʃ/ (fish) · /dʒ/ (juice) vs /j/ (yes) · third-person /s/ /z/ /ɪz/ with food verbs · /æ/ (apple) vs /e/ (bread)
focus_ar: /iː/ مقابل /ɪ/، و /tʃ/ مقابل /ʃ/، و /dʒ/ مقابل /j/، ونهايات الغائب مع أفعال الأكل، و /æ/ مقابل /e/
arabic_challenge: Egyptian Arabic uses /ʒ/ or /g/ for ج, so English /dʒ/ (juice) can drift. Arabic has ش and no /tʃ/, so 'chicken' may become 'shicken'. The /iː/-/ɪ/ contrast returns in high-frequency food words.

isolation.instructions: /iː/ = long, lips spread (meat, tea, cheese). /ɪ/ = short, relaxed (chicken, fish, milk). These are the two most common vowels on a menu.
isolation.instructions_ar: /iː/ طويل والشفاه مبسوطة (meat, tea). /ɪ/ قصير ومسترخي (chicken, fish). أشهر صوتين في قائمة الأكل.

daily_drills.record_this: I eat meat and cheese and I drink tea with dinner. The chicken and the fish are both cheap.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'cheap' then 'chip'. Clearly different? The first is longer with a wider smile.

isolation.instructions: /ʃ/ (fish) is a long, continuous hiss — air flows the whole time. /tʃ/ (cheese) STARTS with a /t/ stop then bursts into /ʃ/. Feel the tiny stop at the beginning of /tʃ/.
isolation.instructions_ar: /ʃ/ صفير مستمر (زي ش). /tʃ/ يبدأ بوقفة /t/ وبعدها ينفجر لـ /ʃ/. حس بالوقفة الصغيرة في أول /tʃ/.

sentence_practice: The fish is fresh and delicious.
I wash the dishes in the kitchen.
daily_drills.record_this: I eat chicken and cheese for lunch. The fish is fresh and delicious. I wash the dishes in the kitchen after every meal.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'chip' and 'ship'. Only the first should have a hard stop at the start.

isolation.instructions: /dʒ/ (juice, orange) is the VOICED partner of /tʃ/ — a stop then a buzzing burst. /j/ (yes, yogurt) has no stop at all; the tongue just glides. Do not swap them.
isolation.instructions_ar: /dʒ/ (juice) هو النسخة المجهورة من /tʃ/ — وقفة ثم انفجار بطنين. /j/ (yes) مفيهاش وقفة خالص، اللسان بيزحلق بس.

sentence_practice: I drink orange juice every day.
daily_drills.record_this: I drink orange juice every day. Yes, I like yogurt and vegetables. Yesterday I had jam with my bread.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'jam' then 'yam'. The first must begin with a firm stop, the second must glide.

isolation.instructions: Apply last week's rule to eating verbs: eats /s/, likes /s/, drinks /s/, wants /s/ — but washes /ɪz/ and finishes /ɪz/ gain a syllable, and loves /z/, has (irregular).
isolation.instructions_ar: طبّق قاعدة الأسبوع اللي فات على أفعال الأكل: eats /s/، likes /s/، لكن washes /ɪz/ بمقطع زائد.

sentence_practice: He eats rice and drinks water.
She likes cheese but prefers fish.
My mother cooks and washes the dishes.
daily_drills.record_this: He eats rice and drinks water. She likes cheese but prefers fish. My mother cooks the food and washes the dishes.
daily_drills.self_check: Only 'washes' and 'finishes' should gain a syllable. Check the rest are single-syllable.

isolation.instructions: /æ/ (apple, sandwich, salad) = mouth wide open, tongue flat and forward. /e/ (bread, egg, breakfast) = mouth half open, a shorter and higher sound. Arabic learners often merge these.
isolation.instructions_ar: /æ/ الفم مفتوح واسع (apple). /e/ الفم نص مفتوح والصوت أقصر وأعلى (bread). كتير بيدمجوا الاتنين.

sentence_practice: I have bread and eggs for breakfast.
I eat an apple and a salad.
Please pass the jam and the lemon.
daily_drills.record_this: I have bread and eggs for breakfast. For lunch I eat an apple, a sandwich and a salad. Please pass the jam and the lemon.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'bad' then 'bed'. Your mouth must be noticeably wider for the first.

challenge_sentences: I eat chicken and cheese for lunch.
The fish is fresh and delicious.
Yes, I drink orange juice with breakfast.
She washes the dishes and finishes the salad.
daily_drills.record_this: I eat chicken and cheese for lunch. The fish is fresh and delicious. Yes, I drink orange juice with my bread and eggs at breakfast. She washes the dishes and finishes the salad.
daily_drills.self_check: Check the four risky sounds: /tʃ/ vs /ʃ/, /dʒ/ vs /j/, /iː/ vs /ɪ/, /æ/ vs /e/.

test_yourself.instructions: Record yourself talking about food. Then listen back and check each sound group.
test_yourself.instructions_ar: سجّل نفسك وانت تتكلم عن الأكل، وبعدين اسمع وراجع كل مجموعة أصوات.
test_yourself.passage: I like food very much. For breakfast I have bread, eggs and cheese, and I drink tea. For lunch I eat chicken with rice, or fish with a salad. My mother cooks delicious meals and washes all the dishes. In the evening I have a sandwich and an apple, and I drink orange juice. Yes, chicken is my favourite. The fish in this shop is fresh and cheap.

sounds_to_check./iː/ vs /ɪ/: eat, meat, tea, cheese, cheap — chicken, fish, milk, dinner, this
sounds_to_check./tʃ/ vs /ʃ/: chicken, cheese, lunch, sandwich, much — fish, fresh, shop, delicious, washes
sounds_to_check./dʒ/ vs /j/: juice, orange, vegetable — yes, yogurt, your
sounds_to_check.third-person endings: eats /s/, likes /s/, drinks /s/, cooks /s/ — washes /ɪz/, finishes /ɪz/
sounds_to_check./æ/ vs /e/: apple, sandwich, salad, have — bread, eggs, breakfast, very

scoring_guide.90_100: 'chicken' and 'fish' are clearly distinct, 'juice' is never 'yuice'. Ready for week 7.
scoring_guide.50_69: 'chip/ship' or 'bad/bed' still merge. Repeat days 2 and 5.
scoring_guide.below_50: Redo days 1-5 slowly with the mirror.

for_arabic_speakers: /tʃ/ does not exist in Arabic. Build it as /t/ + /ʃ/ said quickly together.
Egyptian ج is often /g/ or /ʒ/ — English 'juice' needs the /dʒ/ stop-plus-buzz.
/æ/ vs /e/ (bad/bed) is a meaning-changing pair. Widen the mouth for /æ/.
Keep the third-person -s automatic — 'he eat' is the most common A1 slip.
supplementary_notes.recording_requirement: Record the 'record_this' line daily; compare day 7 with day 1.
